title: Micro-Repair
concept: The smallest way to make up: soften your tone, do one small thing, sit side by side, and say you noticed the impact — before it hardens into something bigger.
whenToUse: When your tone’s getting sharp, something small stung, or a full repair feels like too much right now but waiting will only make it worse. Timing: start within minutes if you can; complete within 24 hours.
steps: Do one small thing — an action, or just own your part.
Sit side by side instead of face to face if that’s easier.
Say you noticed the impact — one sentence, no “but”.
Take one tiny next step — or take a Pause + Return.

phrases.text: One small thing: I can own ___.
I saw that hurt you. I’m sorry for ___.

working: A sharp reply in the kitchen. Within 30 seconds, a softer tone; then the two of them on the sofa, one thing owned, and it’s cleared before bed.
notWorking: Waiting for “the real talk this weekend” while every evening in between stays tense. Skip enough small repairs and the tension just builds.
activity: Pick one small unfinished thing from the last day. Soften, own your part, and ask — start within minutes if you can; complete within 24 hours.
